controls.text: The website has a documented purpose, intended audiences, business outcomes, and measurable success criteria.
A named business owner is accountable for content, legal approvals, budget, and launch decisions.
The project scope distinguishes migration, redesign, new functionality, content work, and deferred work.
Roles are explicit for product ownership, design, development, content, accessibility, security, privacy, SEO, and operations.
Requirements and acceptance criteria are recorded before implementation and remain traceable to delivered pages and features.
The website is risk-classified based on public exposure, administrator access, forms, uploads, payments, sensitive data, and legal claims.
Required legal, privacy, accessibility, advertising, and brand reviews are identified without treating engineering guidance as legal advice.
External vendors, plugins, themes, fonts, analytics tools, embeds, CDNs, form processors, and email services are inventoried and owned.
The repository, work tracker, content ledger, design system, and production CMS each have a documented source-of-truth role.
Material changes use documented approval, release, rollback, and evidence-retention procedures.
A machine-readable inventory covers every current URL, status code, canonical URL, indexability state, and content type.
Every page is mapped to an approved template or documented exception rather than recreated as an ungoverned one-off design.
Images, documents, video, fonts, logos, icons, and downloadable assets are inventoried with ownership, license, source, and replacement status.
Current titles, descriptions, headings, structured data, internal links, canonicals, robots directives, and sitemap membership are captured before migration.
Forms, scheduling, email marketing, maps, search, payments, downloads, and other functional integrations are inventoried end to end.
All analytics, advertising, tag-manager, session-recording, chat, and tracking scripts are inventoried, deduplicated, and assigned a business purpose.
The current site's accessibility baseline is documented using automated checks plus keyboard, zoom, and assistive-technology sampling.
The current site's performance baseline records representative mobile and desktop lab results and available field data.
A data-flow record shows what users submit, where data goes, who receives it, how long it remains, and how deletion occurs.
A migration ledger contains one row per old URL with its intended destination, action, owner, content status, redirect status, QA evidence, and approval.
Development, staging, and production are separated, named, access-controlled, and protected from accidental cross-environment actions.
Staging is password-protected in addition to using noindex, and it contains no unnecessary production personal or confidential data.
Production deployments are reproducible from versioned source or an exported, reviewable configuration rather than undocumented dashboard edits.
The platform responsibility model states what the host secures and backs up and what the operating organization must configure, test, monitor, and recover.
Themes, plugins, blocks, and libraries are selected for active maintenance, accessibility, compatibility, support, and minimal privilege.
The site uses the smallest practical dependency and plugin set; overlapping plugins and duplicate platform features are avoided.
Failures of external services such as forms, email, maps, analytics, fonts, scheduling, or payment providers degrade safely.
Environment-specific domains, IDs, API endpoints, keys, caching behavior, robots rules, and feature settings are documented without exposing secrets.
Backups cover database, uploads, theme or custom code, configuration, and necessary external exports, and restoration is tested.
A rollback procedure identifies the prior deploy, database or content implications, DNS fallback, responsible person, and verification steps.
Custom theme code, patterns, templates, scripts, styles, configuration, and documentation are version-controlled in an identified repository.
Generated artifacts are distinguishable from authoritative source and can be reproduced by documented commands.
Changes use short-lived branches, focused commits, reviewable diffs, pull requests, and documented verification evidence.
Dependencies and build tools are pinned or locked, reviewed before introduction, and updated through an intentional process.
Formatting, linting, validation, and static analysis run consistently locally and in continuous integration where code is deployed.
Repositories, build output, browser code, CMS fields, screenshots, logs, and documentation contain no secrets or private production data.
Pages use semantic header, navigation, main, article, aside, and footer structures appropriate to the content.
Markup has valid nesting, unique IDs, correctly associated labels, and no duplicate or malformed interactive controls.
Each page has one clear primary heading and a logical heading hierarchy that reflects document structure rather than visual size.
Links navigate, buttons perform actions, and custom controls are not used where native HTML provides the required behavior.
Core content, navigation, and forms remain usable under progressive enhancement when nonessential JavaScript fails.
Reusable templates avoid inline event handlers, arbitrary inline styles, copied script fragments, and page-specific code that bypasses the design system.
External links, downloads, new-window behavior, and target attributes are deliberate, understandable, and safely configured.
Every document includes an appropriate doctype, language, character encoding, viewport configuration, title, and core metadata.
Structured data is generated from truthful visible content and passes the relevant validator without unsupported claims.
A single versioned design-token source governs colors, typography, spacing, radii, borders, shadows, widths, and motion values.
Tokens use semantic names such as text, surface, action, focus, success, warning, and danger rather than page-specific or arbitrary names.
Typography uses a documented scale, limited font families and weights, readable line lengths, and predictable heading and body roles.
Spacing uses a documented scale; repeated arbitrary pixel values and one-off margins are treated as defects.
Breakpoints respond to content failure points and are centralized rather than copied inconsistently across components.
Selectors are component- or block-scoped and avoid names likely to collide with WordPress, plugins, Bootstrap, embeds, or future features.
Specificity stays intentionally low using classes and appropriate :where() grouping so overrides do not become a specificity contest.
ID selectors and !important are prohibited except for a documented, narrow compatibility exception with an owner and removal condition.
Broad element selectors do not unintentionally restyle admin interfaces, embedded tools, plugin components, form controls, or third-party widgets.
Every interactive component defines default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, loading, error, and success states as applicable.
Focus indicators are clearly visible, meet contrast expectations, are not clipped, and are not removed without an accessible replacement.
Text links remain identifiable without relying only on color, and visited-link behavior is deliberate where it improves orientation.
Layouts reflow without unintended horizontal scrolling, overlap, clipping, unreadable text, or touch targets that collapse at narrow widths.
Motion is purposeful, avoids harmful flashing, and respects prefers-reduced-motion without hiding information or functionality.
Duplicate, dead, and superseded CSS is removed; the stylesheet has an enforced size budget and documented ownership.
WCAG 2.2 Level AA is the engineering baseline unless a stricter contractual or legal requirement applies.
Accessibility is implemented in native structure, content, and interaction; an overlay or widget is never accepted as a substitute for remediation.
All navigation, controls, dialogs, menus, forms, and media can be operated with a keyboard alone.
A visible-on-focus skip link reaches the main content, and repeated blocks can be bypassed efficiently.
Landmarks and accessible names let assistive-technology users identify navigation, search, main content, complementary content, and footer regions.
Interactive components expose correct accessible names, roles, values, states, descriptions, and status changes.
Focus order follows the meaningful reading and interaction sequence, and focus is restored or moved intentionally after dynamic actions.
Content remains usable at 200 percent text zoom and through responsive reflow equivalent to 400 percent zoom at standard desktop width.
Text, large text, controls, focus indicators, charts, and meaningful graphics meet applicable contrast requirements.
Color, position, shape, sound, or animation is not the sole way to communicate meaning, state, validation, or required action.
Informative images have concise purpose-based alternative text rather than filenames, keyword stuffing, or redundant visible captions.
Decorative images use empty alternative text or an equivalent mechanism so assistive technology can ignore them.
Form fields have persistent labels, instructions, required-state communication, appropriate autocomplete values, and accessible grouping.
Validation identifies errors in text, associates messages with fields, preserves input, moves focus appropriately, and announces status.
Interactive targets provide sufficient size and spacing, including on touch screens and at responsive breakpoints.
Navigation, labels, component behavior, and help mechanisms remain consistent across templates and processes.
Prerecorded media includes accurate captions and necessary transcripts or audio description; autoplay is avoided.
Dialogs, disclosures, carousels, menus, accordions, and tabs follow established accessible interaction patterns or are replaced with simpler native controls.
Release testing includes manual keyboard, zoom, high-contrast or forced-color, and screen-reader checks on representative complete processes.
The site provides an accurate accessibility statement and contact path without making an unsupported conformance or legal-compliance claim.
HTTPS is enforced for all traffic, mixed content is absent, certificates are monitored, and HSTS is evaluated and configured safely.
Applicable response headers are deliberately configured and verified, including CSP or a staged CSP plan, frame protection, referrer policy, MIME sniffing protection, and permissions policy.
Every privileged CMS, hosting, registrar, DNS, analytics, email, and integration account uses multi-factor authentication or passkeys where supported.
Administrators use unique named accounts, least-privilege roles, no shared credentials, and separate daily-use and privileged access where practical.
Privileged access and active sessions are inventoried, reviewed periodically, and revoked promptly when no longer needed.
Login, password-reset, form, search, and expensive public endpoints have appropriate rate limiting and abuse detection.
WordPress core, themes, plugins, PHP, build tools, and dependencies receive supported security updates through a monitored process.
Each plugin and theme has a documented purpose, vendor, maintenance status, data access, permissions, update owner, and removal plan.
Unused, abandoned, duplicated, or disabled plugins and themes are removed rather than left installed.
Dashboard code editing, arbitrary code execution, unsafe uploads, and unnecessary remote interfaces are disabled or restricted where the platform permits.
All untrusted input is validated and normalized; output is escaped for its context; database access uses safe platform APIs or parameterization.
State-changing requests use WordPress nonces or equivalent CSRF protections in addition to authorization checks.
XSS exposure is reduced through safe templating and sanitization, with Content Security Policy used as defense in depth rather than the only control.
Production errors do not expose stack traces, filesystem paths, SQL details, tokens, or personal data, and security logs avoid sensitive content.
Security events, file or configuration changes, uptime, certificates, and vendor alerts are monitored under a documented incident-response process.
Forms collect only information necessary for the stated purpose and avoid open-ended requests for sensitive or confidential detail when it is not required.
Each collection point provides a clear purpose, recipient, expected response, privacy notice, and any required terms or acknowledgments.
Professional-service intake forms clearly warn users not to submit confidential or emergency information until the responsible business and legal owners approve different language.
Form validation runs on the server or trusted service, rejects unexpected fields and values, and does not rely only on browser validation.
Spam, bot, credential-stuffing, and submission abuse controls are proportionate, accessible, rate-limited, and tested for false positives.
File uploads, if allowed, restrict type, size, quantity, filename handling, storage, retrieval authorization, retention, and malware risk.
Submission data is encrypted in transit and protected at rest by the platform and downstream services appropriate to its sensitivity.
Email and chat notifications minimize submitted data, avoid credentials and sensitive attachments, and direct authorized staff to the protected source record.
Retention, deletion, correction, export, backup persistence, and legal-hold behavior are documented and implementable.
Access to submissions is least-privilege, auditable, periodically reviewed, and revoked promptly when roles change.
Cookie, storage, advertising, and nonessential tracking behavior follows an approved consent and privacy design appropriate to applicable requirements.
Analytics tags and properties are deduplicated, documented, tested, filtered for internal traffic as appropriate, and prevented from collecting prohibited data.
Session recording, heatmaps, chat, and replay tools receive explicit privacy, masking, consent, performance, and vendor review before activation.
Third-party processors have documented data flows, retention, security, subprocessor, regional, contract, deletion, and incident considerations.
Every form and integration is tested end to end for success, validation failure, provider outage, duplicate submission, retry, notification, storage, and user-facing recovery.
The project defines measurable page-weight, request-count, JavaScript, CSS, image, font, and third-party performance budgets.
Representative page groups target a 75th-percentile Largest Contentful Paint of 2.5 seconds or less using field data when available.
Representative page groups target a 75th-percentile Interaction to Next Paint of 200 milliseconds or less using field data when available.
Representative page groups target a 75th-percentile Cumulative Layout Shift of 0.1 or less using field data when available.
Images use appropriate formats, dimensions, compression, responsive srcset or sizes, and an intentional media-derivative policy.
Images and embeds reserve dimensions to prevent layout shift; below-the-fold media is lazy-loaded without delaying the likely LCP element.
Fonts are licensed, minimized by family and weight, served under an approved privacy strategy, and loaded without prolonged invisible text.
CSS and JavaScript are minimized, split or deferred when useful, and do not block rendering or ship unused framework payloads without justification.
Caching, CDN behavior, compression, cache invalidation, and authenticated-page exclusions are configured and verified rather than assumed.
Every third-party script has a business owner, consent classification, loading strategy, failure behavior, performance cost, and removal trigger.
The critical user journey remains understandable during slow networks, blocked third-party requests, unavailable embeds, and JavaScript errors.
Templates avoid excessive DOM depth, duplicated hidden markup, unnecessary wrappers, and layout techniques that cause repeated reflow.
Helpful 404, empty, unavailable, validation, and error states preserve navigation and avoid false success messages.
External monitoring covers uptime, TLS, domain expiration, critical forms, and other business-critical journeys with actionable alerts.
Load and resilience testing are proportionate to expected traffic, campaign spikes, bot exposure, and the cost of dependent services.
Every page and reusable content type has a named content owner, purpose, intended audience, update trigger, and review date.
Professional, legal, medical, financial, statistical, testimonial, case-result, and advertising claims receive qualified factual and policy review.
Each indexable page provides distinct, useful, audience-centered value and is not a thin, duplicated, doorway, or keyword-swapped page.
Titles, primary headings, descriptions, link text, and social metadata are accurate, unique where appropriate, and generated from controlled rules.
Each indexable page has one intended canonical URL, and protocol, host, trailing-slash, parameter, archive, and duplicate variants resolve consistently.
Robots directives, sitemap contents, crawl access, feeds, and indexability are intentional for every environment and content type.
Internal navigation and contextual links expose important content, avoid orphan pages, and use understandable link text.
Organization, person, local business, article, breadcrumb, FAQ, review, and other structured data are used only when supported by visible truthful content and current eligibility rules.
Existing URLs are preserved when practical; URL changes require a documented business reason rather than aesthetic preference.
The redirect plan covers every old URL that will not return the intended content at the same URL, including assets and important external campaign links where relevant.
Each redirect is permanent when appropriate, reaches the closest relevant final URL in one hop, preserves necessary parameters, and ends at a successful indexable response.
Staging protections are verified before content entry and fully removed at launch; production noindex, blocked resources, and placeholder canonicals are release blockers.
Migrated images and documents use owned URLs, correct file types and dimensions, useful filenames where practical, accessible text alternatives, and tested inbound links.
Prelaunch and postlaunch crawls compare old and new inventories for status codes, redirects, canonicals, titles, headings, metadata, indexability, internal links, and missing assets.
Search Console, analytics, rankings for material queries, crawl errors, sitemap processing, index coverage, and important landing pages are monitored after launch with an escalation owner.
A risk-based test matrix covers every template, content type, critical journey, supported browser, viewport class, input method, and relevant user state.
Automated checks cover formatting, linting, build integrity, HTML or template validation, links, accessibility, security, and performance where the stack permits.
Manual release testing covers keyboard operation, zoom and reflow, representative screen-reader use, focus behavior, and complete user processes.
All forms, scheduling, downloads, search, payments, email, analytics, consent, maps, and third-party integrations are tested in their production-like configuration.
Visual regression or disciplined template screenshots detect unintended layout, typography, responsive, and content changes across releases.
Prelaunch security review covers privileged accounts, multi-factor authentication, access, updates, plugins, headers, forms, secrets, logging, backups, and recovery.
A complete content and technical crawl is reconciled against the migration ledger before approval, with no unexplained URL or asset omissions.
The release plan defines change freeze, backup, deployment steps, DNS actions, verification, rollback thresholds, owners, and communication.
Postlaunch smoke tests and monitoring begin immediately and continue through a defined stabilization period before legacy hosting or rollback options are removed.
Active production websites receive a complete 150-control review at least quarterly, with affected controls reviewed for every material change and evidence retained.
